title: CISB-Bench
summary: Building auditable source and intermediate-representation evidence for studying security bugs introduced by compilers.
research:
Compiler optimizations transform programs in ways that can be difficult to inspect from source code alone. CISB-Bench supports research on compiler-introduced security bugs by connecting small C programs with compiler provenance, intermediate-representation artifacts, and documented evidence for security labels.

The dataset brings together cases mined from GCC and LLVM and retains both security-positive cases and challenging non-CISB examples. Its construction combines repository mining, candidate filtering, independent review, adjudication, and annotations describing the relevant mechanisms and boundaries. These records allow researchers to inspect why a case received a label and what evidence supports that decision.

Our research uses this foundation to evaluate compiler-security detection and analysis methods, including approaches that combine language models with program-analysis evidence. We examine reproducibility, label validity, and the trade-offs between finding relevant bugs and producing unsupported security claims. The aim is a reusable basis for comparing methods and improving the reliability of compiler-security research.
